gameplayTips.title: Quicken & Quickbloom
gameplayTips.rawContentMarkdown: [[note:tips-quickbloom]]
gameplayTips.renderedHtml:
Applying Electro & Dendro on the same enemy creates a Quicken aura.
Applying Electro on a Quicken aura triggers the Aggravate reaction.

Applying Hydro & Dendro on the same enemy triggers a Bloom reaction and creates a Dendro core.
Applying Electro on a Dendro core triggers the Hyperbloom reaction.

A team featuring both the Aggrave & Hyperbloom reactions is referred to as Quickbloom.

notes.rawMarkdown: [[character:arataki-itto]] is a [[element:geo]] DPS Character who takes advantage of his [[ability:burst]]'s [[stat:atk|ATK]] boost and [[element:geo]] infusion to deal significant damage during its uptime. His combos involve stacking and unleashing his [[ability:ca|Charged Attacks]], named Arataki Kesagiri. Arataki Kesagiri consumes no stamina and can be cast continuously as long as he has Superlative Superstrength stacks. Superlative Superstrength is capped at 5 stacks at any given time, and [[character:arataki-itto]] gets those stacks when his 2nd and 4th [[ability:na]] string hits an enemy. Activating his [[ability:burst]] allows his 1st and 3rd [[ability:na|Normal Attack]] to also generate stacks. [[character:arataki-itto]]'s [[ability:skill]] deals damage to enemies on cast and summons a taunt, Ushi, which is considered a [[element:geo]] Construct. This initial cast damage grants [[character:arataki-itto]] 1 Superlative Superstrength stack, and upon Ushi leaving the field, [[character:arataki-itto]] is granted another stack. When Ushi takes damage, [[character:arataki-itto]] gains a stack (capped at 1 stack per 2 seconds). [[character:arataki-itto]]'s [[ability:burst]] converts his [[ability:na|Normal]] and [[ability:ca|Charged Attacks]] into [[stat:geo-dmg]], increases [[character:arataki-itto]]'s [[ability:na|Normal Attack]] Speed and converts a portion of [[character:arataki-itto]]'s current [[stat:def|DEF]] to [[stat:atk|ATK]].
notes.renderedHtml: Arataki Itto is a Geo DPS Character who takes advantage of his Burst's ATK boost and Geo infusion to deal significant damage during its uptime. His combos involve stacking and unleashing his Charged Attacks, named Arataki Kesagiri. Arataki Kesagiri consumes no stamina and can be cast continuously as long as he has Superlative Superstrength stacks. Superlative Superstrength is capped at 5 stacks at any given time, and Arataki Itto gets those stacks when his 2nd and 4th Normal Attack string hits an enemy. Activating his Burst allows his 1st and 3rd Normal Attack to also generate stacks. Arataki Itto's Skill deals damage to enemies on cast and summons a taunt, Ushi, which is considered a Geo Construct. This initial cast damage grants Arataki Itto 1 Superlative Superstrength stack, and upon Ushi leaving the field, Arataki Itto is granted another stack. When Ushi takes damage, Arataki Itto gains a stack (capped at 1 stack per 2 seconds). Arataki Itto's Burst converts his Normal and Charged Attacks into Geo DMG, increases Arataki Itto's Normal Attack Speed and converts a portion of Arataki Itto's current DEF to ATK.

gameplayTips.title: Bond of Life
gameplayTips.rawContentMarkdown: [[note:tips-bol]]
gameplayTips.renderedHtml: Bond of Life is a mechanic that absorbs any healing a character receives. It appears as a red outline around their HP bar, and its maximum value is 200% of the character's HP (represented by an outline around the entire HP bar). To clear a Bond of Life, the character must receive healing equal to its value.

notes.rawMarkdown: [[character:clorinde]] is a DPS who primarily deals damage with her [[ability:skill]], which puts her into a special state that **infuses her [[ability:na]]s with [[element:electro]]**, and grants her a [[ability:bol]] for each [[ability:na]] performed. She can then **use her [[ability:skill]] again** to consume that [[ability:bol]], **increasing that attack's damage** depending on its amount, and **heal herself**. While in that state, healing from sources other than her [[ability:skill]] **increases [[character:clorinde]]'s [[ability:bol]] instead of restoring her HP**. [[character:clorinde]]'s [[ability:burst]] also grants her a [[ability:bol]], with the amount increasing based on her talent level.
notes.renderedHtml: Clorinde is a DPS who primarily deals damage with her Skill, which puts her into a special state that infuses her Normal Attacks with Electro, and grants her a Bond of Life for each Normal Attack performed. She can then use her Skill again to consume that Bond of Life, increasing that attack's damage depending on its amount, and heal herself. While in that state, healing from sources other than her Skill increases Clorinde's Bond of Life instead of restoring her HP. Clorinde's Burst also grants her a Bond of Life, with the amount increasing based on her talent level.

notes.rawMarkdown: [[character:clorinde]]'s fast and frequent [[element:electro]] attacks make her a great fit for teams with [[element:dendro]] characters (notably [[character:nahida]]), using the **[[element:aggravate]] and/or [[element:hyperbloom]] reaction** to deal extra damage.
notes.renderedHtml: Clorinde's fast and frequent Electro attacks make her a great fit for teams with Dendro characters (notably Nahida), using the Aggravate and/or Hyperbloom reaction to deal extra damage.

gameplayTips.title: Bond of Life
gameplayTips.rawContentMarkdown: [[note:tips-bol]]
gameplayTips.renderedHtml: Bond of Life is a mechanic that absorbs any healing a character receives. It appears as a red outline around their HP bar, and its maximum value is 200% of the character's HP (represented by an outline around the entire HP bar). To clear a Bond of Life, the character must receive healing equal to its value.

gameplayTips.title: Aggravate & Quickbloom
gameplayTips.rawContentMarkdown: [[note:tips-quickbloom]]
gameplayTips.renderedHtml:
Applying Electro & Dendro on the same enemy creates a Quicken aura.
Applying Electro on a Quicken aura triggers the Aggravate reaction.

Applying Hydro & Dendro on the same enemy triggers a Bloom reaction and creates a Dendro core.
Applying Electro on a Dendro core triggers the Hyperbloom reaction.

A team featuring both the Aggrave & Hyperbloom reactions is referred to as Quickbloom.

notes.renderedHtml: Furina can act as both an Off-Field DPS through her Skill and a Buff Support through her Burst.

notes.rawMarkdown:
Her kit revolves around **[[stat:hp|HP]] variations**: her [[ability:skill]] summons pets that deal [[element:hydro]] DMG and drain your team's [[stat:hp|HP]] **(as long as they are above 50%)** to increase their damage. Her [[ability:burst]] buffs your team's DMG% based on the amount of [[stat:hp|HP]] gained or lost by your team, with each percentage point counting towards its stacks.
Because of this, **playing her with a healer is recommended, preferably a teamwide one**. This allows you to keep your team above 50% [[stat:hp|HP]] while letting her pets drain their [[stat:hp|HP]], generating the [[stat:hp|HP]] variation needed to build [[ability:burst]] stacks.
notes.renderedHtml:
Her kit revolves around HP variations: her Skill summons pets that deal Hydro DMG and drain your team's HP (as long as they are above 50%) to increase their damage. Her Burst buffs your team's DMG% based on the amount of HP gained or lost by your team, with each percentage point counting towards its stacks.
Because of this, playing her with a healer is recommended, preferably a teamwide one. This allows you to keep your team above 50% HP while letting her pets drain their HP, generating the HP variation needed to build Burst stacks.

notes.rawMarkdown: [[character:furina]] can also switch mode by using her [[ability:ca]]: this will replace her attacking pets by a healing pet that heals your active character. However, this removes all of her off-field damage, [[element:hydro]] application and energy generation, making this mode **generally not recommended** unless you need to temporarily switch her [[ability:arkhe]] alignment.
notes.renderedHtml: Furina can also switch mode by using her Charged Attack: this will replace her attacking pets by a healing pet that heals your active character. However, this removes all of her off-field damage, Hydro application and energy generation, making this mode generally not recommended unless you need to temporarily switch her Arkhe alignment.

notes.rawMarkdown: [[character:furina]] **defaults to high energy requirements in most teams**. Some factors (including but not limited to [[element:hydro]] teammates, [[character:shogun-raiden]], Favonius weapons) can allow her to run low energy requirement builds: it’s best to consult the **[Energy Recharge Calculator](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-vkmgp5n0bI9pvhUg110Aza3Emb2puLWdeoCgrxDlu4/edit?gid=613391376#gid=613391376)** to see what build is right for you.
notes.renderedHtml: Furina defaults to high energy requirements in most teams. Some factors (including but not limited to Hydro teammates, Raiden Shogun, Favonius weapons) can allow her to run low energy requirement builds: it’s best to consult the Energy Recharge Calculator to see what build is right for you.

gameplayTips.title: DMG% buff
gameplayTips.rawContentMarkdown:
At [C0], [[character:furina]]'s [[ability:burst]] can provide up to 75% DMG% Bonus, which is the **equivalent of 1,6 DMG% Goblet**. As such, DPS characters played with her may want to use their **scaling stats instead of a DMG% Goblet**.
DPS that rely on reactions that do not scale on DMG% (such as **Lunar or [[element:stellar-glimmer]] reactions**) however wont benefit from her [[ability:burst]]'s buff, and thus **should not be played with her**.
gameplayTips.renderedHtml:
At [C0], Furina's Burst can provide up to 75% DMG% Bonus, which is the equivalent of 1,6 DMG% Goblet. As such, DPS characters played with her may want to use their scaling stats instead of a DMG% Goblet.
DPS that rely on reactions that do not scale on DMG% (such as Lunar or Stellar Glimmer reactions) however wont benefit from her Burst's buff, and thus should not be played with her.

gameplayTips.title: Marechaussee Hunter
gameplayTips.rawContentMarkdown: Thanks to her [[ability:skill]] causing your **entire team's [[stat:hp|HP]] to vary often**, [[character:furina]] enables On-Field DPS characters whose [[stat:hp|HP]] would not normally vary during combat to use **[[set:marechaussee-hunter]] (4)**.
gameplayTips.renderedHtml: Thanks to her Skill causing your entire team's HP to vary often, Furina enables On-Field DPS characters whose HP would not normally vary during combat to use Marechaussee Hunter (4).

gameplayTips.title: Pets targetting
gameplayTips.rawContentMarkdown:
[[character:furina]]'s [[ability:skill]] pets will prioritize attacking **the target of your active character**. If it doesnt have a target, they will instead attack the **nearest enemy**.
When facing multiple enemies, you can identify which one the pets are targeting by looking for the **white arrow displayed above its [[stat:hp|HP]] bar**.
gameplayTips.renderedHtml:
Furina's Skill pets will prioritize attacking the target of your active character. If it doesnt have a target, they will instead attack the nearest enemy.
When facing multiple enemies, you can identify which one the pets are targeting by looking for the white arrow displayed above its HP bar.

notes.rawMarkdown: [[character:furina]] can act as both an **Off-Field DPS** through her [[ability:skill]] and a **Buff Support** through her [[ability:burst]].
notes.renderedHtml: Furina can act as both an Off-Field DPS through her Skill and a Buff Support through her Burst.

notes.rawMarkdown:
Her kit revolves around **[[stat:hp|HP]] variations**: her [[ability:skill]] summons pets that deal [[element:hydro]] DMG and drain your team's [[stat:hp|HP]] **(as long as they are above 50%)** to increase their damage. Her [[ability:burst]] buffs your team's DMG% based on the amount of [[stat:hp|HP]] gained or lost by your team, with each percentage point counting towards its stacks.
Because of this, **playing her with a healer is recommended, preferably a teamwide one**. This allows you to keep your team above 50% [[stat:hp|HP]] while letting her pets drain their [[stat:hp|HP]], generating the [[stat:hp|HP]] variation needed to build [[ability:burst]] stacks.
notes.renderedHtml:
Her kit revolves around HP variations: her Skill summons pets that deal Hydro DMG and drain your team's HP (as long as they are above 50%) to increase their damage. Her Burst buffs your team's DMG% based on the amount of HP gained or lost by your team, with each percentage point counting towards its stacks.
Because of this, playing her with a healer is recommended, preferably a teamwide one. This allows you to keep your team above 50% HP while letting her pets drain their HP, generating the HP variation needed to build Burst stacks.

notes.rawMarkdown: [[character:furina]] can also switch mode by using her [[ability:ca]]: this will replace her attacking pets by a healing pet that heals your active character. However, this removes all of her off-field damage, [[element:hydro]] application and energy generation, making this mode **generally not recommended** unless you need to temporarily switch her [[ability:arkhe]] alignment.
notes.renderedHtml: Furina can also switch mode by using her Charged Attack: this will replace her attacking pets by a healing pet that heals your active character. However, this removes all of her off-field damage, Hydro application and energy generation, making this mode generally not recommended unless you need to temporarily switch her Arkhe alignment.

notes.rawMarkdown: [[character:furina]] **defaults to high energy requirements in most teams**. Some factors (including but not limited to [[element:hydro]] teammates, [[character:shogun-raiden]], Favonius weapons) can allow her to run low energy requirement builds: it’s best to consult the **[Energy Recharge Calculator](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-vkmgp5n0bI9pvhUg110Aza3Emb2puLWdeoCgrxDlu4/edit?gid=613391376#gid=613391376)** to see what build is right for you.
notes.renderedHtml: Furina defaults to high energy requirements in most teams. Some factors (including but not limited to Hydro teammates, Raiden Shogun, Favonius weapons) can allow her to run low energy requirement builds: it’s best to consult the Energy Recharge Calculator to see what build is right for you.

gameplayTips.title: DMG% buff
gameplayTips.rawContentMarkdown:
At [C0], [[character:furina]]'s [[ability:burst]] can provide up to 75% DMG% Bonus, which is the **equivalent of 1,6 DMG% Goblet**. As such, DPS characters played with her may want to use their **scaling stats instead of a DMG% Goblet**.
DPS that rely on reactions that do not scale on DMG% (such as **Lunar or [[element:stellar-glimmer]] reactions**) however wont benefit from her [[ability:burst]]'s buff, and thus **should not be played with her**.
gameplayTips.renderedHtml:
At [C0], Furina's Burst can provide up to 75% DMG% Bonus, which is the equivalent of 1,6 DMG% Goblet. As such, DPS characters played with her may want to use their scaling stats instead of a DMG% Goblet.
DPS that rely on reactions that do not scale on DMG% (such as Lunar or Stellar Glimmer reactions) however wont benefit from her Burst's buff, and thus should not be played with her.

gameplayTips.title: Marechaussee Hunter
gameplayTips.rawContentMarkdown: Thanks to her [[ability:skill]] causing your **entire team's [[stat:hp|HP]] to vary often**, [[character:furina]] enables On-Field DPS characters whose [[stat:hp|HP]] would not normally vary during combat to use **[[set:marechaussee-hunter]] (4)**.
gameplayTips.renderedHtml: Thanks to her Skill causing your entire team's HP to vary often, Furina enables On-Field DPS characters whose HP would not normally vary during combat to use Marechaussee Hunter (4).

gameplayTips.title: Pets targeting
gameplayTips.rawContentMarkdown:
[[character:furina]]'s [[ability:skill]] pets will prioritize attacking **the target of your active character**. If it doesnt have a target, they will instead attack the **nearest enemy**.
When facing multiple enemies, you can identify which one the pets are targeting by looking for the **white arrow displayed above its [[stat:hp|HP]] bar**.
gameplayTips.renderedHtml:
Furina's Skill pets will prioritize attacking the target of your active character. If it doesnt have a target, they will instead attack the nearest enemy.
When facing multiple enemies, you can identify which one the pets are targeting by looking for the white arrow displayed above its HP bar.

sectionNotes: While typically Jean will heal enough that you do not need to try and build for as much healing as possible, when paired with Furina it can be beneficial swapping to an ATK% goblet and Healing Bonus circlet. This is to aid in building Fanfare points faster, and Jean's personal damage is not particularly significant to begin with. When building Jean in such a way, prioritize weapons which provide ATK% or Energy Recharge. If using Favonius Sword, a CRIT Rate circlet can be taken to ensure more consistent procs.

gameplayTips.title: Quickbloom
gameplayTips.rawContentMarkdown: [[note:tips-quickbloom]]
gameplayTips.renderedHtml:
Applying Electro & Dendro on the same enemy creates a Quicken aura.
Applying Electro on a Quicken aura triggers the Aggravate reaction.

Applying Hydro & Dendro on the same enemy triggers a Bloom reaction and creates a Dendro core.
Applying Electro on a Dendro core triggers the Hyperbloom reaction.

A team featuring both the Aggrave & Hyperbloom reactions is referred to as Quickbloom.

notes.rawMarkdown: [[character:navia]] is a DPS that can frontload a significant portion of her damage with her [[ability:skill]]. To maximize her [[ability:skill]] damage, she utilizes Crystal Shrapnel stacks gained from picking up [[element:crystallize]] shards or triggering a [[element:lunar-crystallize]] reaction. While her [[ability:burst]] is active, it grants additional stacks. Because of this, it is important to be able to use her [[ability:burst]] every rotation and to have off-field [[element:pyro]]/[[element:hydro]]/[[element:electro]]/[[element:cryo]] application to increase the amount of [[element:crystallize]] shards.
notes.renderedHtml: Navia is a DPS that can frontload a significant portion of her damage with her Skill. To maximize her Skill damage, she utilizes Crystal Shrapnel stacks gained from picking up Crystallize shards or triggering a Lunar-Crystallize reaction. While her Burst is active, it grants additional stacks. Because of this, it is important to be able to use her Burst every rotation and to have off-field Pyro/Hydro/Electro/Cryo application to increase the amount of Crystallize shards.

notes.rawMarkdown: After using her [[ability:skill]], [[character:navia]] gains 4 seconds of [[element:geo]] infusion, allowing her to deal additional damage and build up Crystal Shrapnel stacks for the next [[ability:skill]]. The [[ability:burst]] should be used before her field-time to maximize the stack generation.
notes.renderedHtml: After using her Skill, Navia gains 4 seconds of Geo infusion, allowing her to deal additional damage and build up Crystal Shrapnel stacks for the next Skill. The Burst should be used before her field-time to maximize the stack generation.

notes.rawMarkdown: Full Combo: {rot:Q} …(Swap to teammates)… {rot:E N3D N2 E N3D N2}. You can swap off [[character:navia]] before second [[ability:skill]] if you have characters which could insert quick ability casts, such as [[character:xilonen]]. Last 2 [[ability:na]]s can be skipped in teams with fast rotations. Depending on the uptime of other characters in the team, [[ability:burst]] can be used closer to the start of the rotation or closer to [[character:navia]]'s fieldtime.

notes.rawMarkdown: [[character:prune]] is a support that relies on triggering the [[element:swirl]] reaction to buff characters. Triggering [[element:swirl]] will convert her Banehunter Oathhammer ([[ability:skill]]) into the element she Swirls, and as long as her A4 talent is unlocked, hitting opponents with a converted Banehunter Oathhammer or her [[ability:burst]] will activate the Tolling Rally effect, which will provide DMG buffs to the team based on [[character:prune]]'s [[stat:atk|ATK]]. In addition, when a [[ability:hexerei]] character under Tolling Rally triggers a reaction, [[character:prune]] gains an [[stat:atk%]] boost, and if that reaction was [[element:swirl]], the triggering character also gains an [[stat:atk%]] boost.
notes.renderedHtml: Prune is a support that relies on triggering the Swirl reaction to buff characters. Triggering Swirl will convert her Banehunter Oathhammer (Skill) into the element she Swirls, and as long as her A4 talent is unlocked, hitting opponents with a converted Banehunter Oathhammer or her Burst will activate the Tolling Rally effect, which will provide DMG buffs to the team based on Prune's ATK. In addition, when a Hexerei character under Tolling Rally triggers a reaction, Prune gains an ATK% boost, and if that reaction was Swirl, the triggering character also gains an ATK% boost.

notes.rawMarkdown: [[character:prune]]'s [C1] let's her restore 2 Energy every 1.8 seconds whenever a converted Banehunter Oathhammer hits opponents. How much total energy she can restore depends how often [[character:prune]] is able to trigger [[element:swirl]] during the duration of her [[ability:burst]]. [[character:prune]]'s [C6] increases her [[ability:burst]] duration by 4 seconds.
notes.renderedHtml: Prune's [C1] let's her restore 2 Energy every 1.8 seconds whenever a converted Banehunter Oathhammer hits opponents. How much total energy she can restore depends how often Prune is able to trigger Swirl during the duration of her Burst. Prune's [C6] increases her Burst duration by 4 seconds.

There are three recommended combos that [[character:tighnari]] can perform:
1. {rot:E C Q 2C} - This is the most mechanically difficult combo. However, this combo allows [[character:tighnari]] to have both his [[ability:burst]] affected by A1 and funnel particles from his [[ability:skill]] to his next [[ability:burst]].

3. {rot:E Q 3C} - Simplest combo to use, and generally weakest combo though it allows prefunneling. His [[ability:burst]] does not benefit from A1 in this combo. It is recommended at [C4] due to the [[stat:em]] buff.

notes.rawMarkdown: **In [[element:freeze]] teams**, she reduces the [[element:hydro]] and [[element:cryo]] RES of opponents hit by her [[ability:skill]]. notes.renderedHtml: In Freeze teams, she reduces the Hydro and Cryo RES of opponents hit by her Skill. In addition, Vodyanitsa's A4 talent also increases the Hydro and Cryo DMG dealt by teammates, which scales based on her Max HP.

These enhanced Vortexes, when generated or exploded, also reduce enemies' [[element:anemo]] RES. Her A4 talent will increase the [[element:stellar-swirl]] damage dealt by teammates, which scales based on her Max [[stat:hp|HP]].
notes.renderedHtml: In Stellar Swirl teams, Vodyanitsa's Skill also enhances any Stellar Vortexes created by the Stellar Swirl reaction. These enhanced Vortexes, when generated or exploded, also reduce enemies' Anemo RES. Her A4 talent will increase the Stellar Swirl damage dealt by teammates, which scales based on her Max HP.

notes.rawMarkdown: Triggering [[element:stellar-swirl]] at least every 8s while [[character:vodyanitsa]]'s [[ability:skill]] is active will prevent her A4 buffs from being applied to [[element:hydro]] and [[element:cryo]] damage, and instead only applied to [[element:stellar-swirl]] damage.
notes.renderedHtml: Triggering Stellar Swirl at least every 8s while Vodyanitsa's Skill is active will prevent her A4 buffs from being applied to Hydro and Cryo damage, and instead only applied to Stellar Swirl damage.

gameplayTips.title: Interruption Resistance
gameplayTips.rawContentMarkdown:
Interruption Resistance can take different forms in a character’s kit. The most obvious is **through a shield**, but some characters **grant it directly without generating one**.

Examples include, but are not limited to, **[[character:xingqiu]]**’s [[ability:burst]], **[[character:vodyanitsa]]**’s [[ability:skill]], and **[[character:xilonen]]**’s [C1].

Not all forms grant **interruption immunity**: Interruption Resistance **reduces the frequency** of getting staggered when hit by attacks, but **does not prevent it**.

items.name: Favonius Lance
items.note: Use this weapon over Black Tassel if you value the team energy (Note that you need to build some amount of CRIT Rate if you are running Favonius Lance to trigger the passive)

items.name: Archaic Petra
items.note: Can be more useful than Tenacity of the Millelith (4) in teams that don't scale as well with ATK buffs or already have another Tenacity of the Millelith holder. Though it can be an awkward set to utilize well without extending rotation times, since the Holder of the set (Zhongli in this case) has to pickup the shard for the buff to take effect.

items.name: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City
items.note: Preferred over Archaic Petra if there are multiple Crystallize-compatible Elements or Geo characters that want DMG% bonus.

items.name: Deepwood Memories
items.note: This set works best in Dendro reaction focused teams (Bloom/Burgeon/Hyperbloom/Spread) that prefer having Deepwood Memories on Zhongli so that they can run more damage focused sets such as Gilded Dreams / Flower of Paradise Lost instead for the highest overall damage gain. That said it means keeping the enemies near your pillars to have good uptime on the Dendro resistance shred effect, which can be difficult with no grouping abilities in a team.

items.name: Instructor
items.note: This set is usually only used in a few heavily reaction focused teams, such as Ganyu Melt or Hu Tao Vape, where you're maximising your damage in exchange for a weaker shield. Though Zhongli's shield is still usually more than strong enough even with fewer substat rolls to strengthen it.

items.name: Tenacity of the Millelith
items.note: This set is best in slot for Shield HP, but it's usually inconsistent against Bosses and needs good Construct placement, due to it's inconsistency, it's better to use other buffing sets that are mentioned if they work for the team.

circlet.name: CRIT Rate
circlet.note: Only recommended if using a Favonius weapon.

notes.rawMarkdown: This kind of playstyle is very straightforward; stack as much HP as possible. Prioritize HP scaling polearms such as **[[weapon:black-tassel]]** and artifact sets such as **[[set:tenacity-of-the-millelith]]** (4) to capitalize on [[character:zhongli]]'s Shield. Most of the time, especially on a HP-focused [[character:zhongli]], casting [[ability:burst]] is a DPS loss due to the cast time, which is why you'd only want to cast [[ability:burst]] for the Crowd Control it offers, and not for damage.
